Tignes Val d'Isère | Linked ski areas | Snow Catchers

How Tignes and Val d'Isère fit together across the Tovière and Bellevarde ridge, which base reaches which side, how the snow changes with height, what the single area pass costs, and what the area is like for boarders, families, food and evenings.

Tignes and Val d'Isère share the head of the Isère valley, joined over the ridge of Tovière and Bellevarde into one area that the operator puts at {{f:F000373}} of piste. Its lifts climb from Les Brévières at {{f:F000382}} to the Grande Motte cable car at {{f:F000381}}. Tignes was built for skiing after its old village vanished under the Chevril reservoir in {{f:F000386}}, and in {{f:F000388}} Val d'Isère staged the Olympic men's downhill on the Face de Bellevarde.

Tignes fills the upper bowl of its valley, from Les Brévières and Tignes 1800 near the Chevril dam up to Le Lac, Le Lavachet and Val Claret around the lake, with the Grande Motte glacier above them. Val d'Isère lies over the ridge to the east, strung out from La Daille through the village to Le Fornet, with Bellevarde and Solaise on either side of it. Lifts from both resorts reach the ridge between Tovière and Bellevarde, and in the map data a skier from Val Claret reaches La Daille in one lift ride and comes back in one.

The link is broad. In the model no single lift closure separates the two resorts, and the worst closures add lift rides rather than cut journeys. Closing the Olympique or the Solaise gondola in the centre of Val d'Isère adds {{f:F000473}} lift rides in total across the journeys between sectors, and closing the Tommeuses chair, the main way up from La Daille to Tignes, adds {{f:F000475}}.

Le Fornet is the exception. Its lifts climb to the Pissaillas glacier, but the only lift out of the sector towards the rest of the area is the Leissières chair to Solaise. If it stops, Le Fornet can still be reached on skis but none of the other {{f:F000472|w}} sectors can be reached from it by lift.

The operator counts {{f:F000374}} runs: {{f:F000375}} green, {{f:F000376}} blue, {{f:F000377}} red and {{f:F000378}} black. skiresort.com measures {{f:F000084}} of the piste as easy, {{f:F000085}} as intermediate and {{f:F000086}} as difficult, the highest difficult share of the four Savoie areas on this site.

Green and blue reach every sector in the map data, but the way round can be long. Between the centres of the two resorts the easy routes cost at most one extra lift ride, while Solaise and Le Fornet are another matter: from Tignes Le Lac, Le Fornet takes {{m:easy.le-lac.le-fornet|w}} lift rides on green and blue against {{m:all.le-lac.le-fornet|w}} with every run allowed.

Black runs matter more here than in the other big Savoie areas. Coming back into Tignes Le Lac and Les Brévières from Val d'Isère, the fewest lift rides use a black run, and staying on reds costs one more ride: from the village of Val d'Isère, Tignes Le Lac takes {{m:all.val-disere.le-lac|w}} lift rides with a black and {{m:red.val-disere.le-lac|w}} without.

The steepest skiing is on the Val d'Isère side. The Face de Bellevarde, the Olympic downhill of {{f:F000388}}, runs from the Rocher de Bellevarde to the village, and the Oreiller-Killy red drops about {{f:F000392}} over just over {{f:F000391}} to La Daille. On the Tignes side the Grande Motte glacier runs fall about {{f:F000393}} to Val Claret when they are fully open.

Most of the skiing starts high. Tignes Le Lac and Val Claret have their lowest lifts at {{f:F000420}} and {{f:F000424}}, and on the elevation model the Grande Motte lifts start at {{f:F000428}} and climb to {{f:F000429}}. The low ground is limited to Les Brévières, La Daille and the village of Val d'Isère, whose lowest lifts start between {{f:F000416|n}} and {{f:F000436}}.

The weather model behind the snowfall figures covers the whole area with one grid cell, so it cannot tell Tignes from Val d'Isère, but it shows plainly what height does. In a typical season between 1991 and 2020, about {{f:F000105}} of snow fell at 1,600 m, {{f:F000478}} at 2,100 m and {{f:F000480}} at 2,600 m.

The lower slopes have lost the most. At 1,600 m the typical season fell from {{f:F000477}} in 1961 to 1990 to {{f:F000105}} in 1991 to 2020, and four of the last five seasons sat in the lowest third of the 76 year record. At 2,600 m the fall was smaller, from {{f:F000481}} to {{f:F000480}}, though three of the last five seasons were that poor.

Height still sets the calendar. Tignes opens on {{f:F000383|dm}}, a week before the link to Val d'Isère on {{f:F000384|dm}}, and the whole area runs to {{f:F000385|dm}}, later than the linked areas of Les 3 Vallées and Paradiski. The model gives snowfall rather than depth on the ground, and measured depths from weather stations are still being collected.

Getting there and choosing a base

By the fastest road, Geneva airport is {{f:F000482}} from Les Brévières and {{f:F000483}} from Le Fornet, Lyon airport {{f:F000484|n}} to {{f:F000485}} and Chambéry {{f:F000486|n}} to {{f:F000487}}. Every route climbs from Bourg-Saint-Maurice on the D902 past the Chevril dam, and the Col de l'Iseran beyond Val d'Isère is closed to traffic in winter, so there is no way in from the Maurienne.

Bourg-Saint-Maurice is the railway station, {{f:F000488|n}} to {{f:F000489}} from the villages by road, and the Eurostar ski service from London calls there on winter Saturdays. Regional buses run from the station to both resorts, and some long distance coaches stop at La Daille, where free shuttles run to the centre of Val d'Isère.

Road distances are the fastest route by the OSRM router on OpenStreetMap data, without traffic or snow. The ski train as reported by Seat 61; roads and buses by Guide Ski. 2026/27 bus timetables have not yet been checked.

Tignes Le Lac and Val Claret are the best placed bases. From Val Claret, Val d'Isère is {{f:F000449|w}} lift rides away and a lift top above 3,000 m only {{f:F000451|w}}, by the Perce-Neige funicular. From the village of Val d'Isère, Tignes Le Lac is {{f:F000456|w}} lift rides away.

Les Brévières and Le Fornet pay for their quiet in lifts. From Les Brévières, Val d'Isère takes {{f:F000465|w}} lift rides and Le Fornet {{f:F000466|w}}; from Le Fornet, Tignes Le Lac takes {{f:F000468|w}}.

Each resort keeps its own park. Tignes has its snowpark at the top of the Grattalu chair above Val Claret, with kickers, rails and boxes for beginners and intermediates and a free airbag, a halfpipe at the foot of the Lanches chair, and an expert boardercross in the same Palet sector. Val d'Isère's Val Park fills the middle of the Bellevarde bowl below the Mont Blanc chair, with kickers graded from green to black.

Drag lifts are scarce in the villages and common on the glacier. In the map data {{f:F000413}} of the {{f:F000412}} main lifts are drags; they make up {{f:F000431}} of the main lifts on the Grande Motte and {{f:F000447}} in Le Fornet, against {{f:F000427}} in Val Claret.
Away from the parks, terrain beyond the markers is not controlled, so the avalanche bulletin and a local guide come first.

Tignes and Val d'Isère both carry the Famille Plus label for family resorts, and the pass is generous to the young: children under 8 ski free, and a family buying four week passes together saves {{f:F000410}} on the total.

Tignes makes the first days easy. Free beginner lifts run at Le Lac, Le Lavachet and Val Claret, the Bollin chair at Val Claret is free, and four free sledging areas sit at Le Lac, Le Lavachet, Tignes 1800 and Les Brévières. The Expédition Cobra snow luge runs about {{f:F000394}} down from Palafour and is not recommended for children under 13, and passes of six days or more include unlimited entry to the Lagon pool.

Val d'Isère has a free drag to the green Savonnette run at the foot of the main snow front, Ski Tranquille slow zones at Solaise and Bellevarde, a snow garden for the youngest, and the Centre Aquasportif with a sports pool and a leisure pool. Free shuttles link La Daille, Le Fornet and Legettaz to the centre.
For a base, Tignes Le Lac has the highest share of green and blue in the map data, {{f:F000422}}, and sits one lift ride from Val Claret, La Daille and Les Brévières.
Sources: France.fr on Famille Plus (updated October 2023), Guide Ski for Tignes and for Val d'Isère. Ages and opening times are best checked when booking.
Each resort has one Michelin star in the 2026 guide: Ursus in Tignes, where Clément Bouvier cooks, and La Table de l'Ours in Val d'Isère, Antoine Gras's restaurant in the Barmes de l'Ours hotel.

On the Val d'Isère side, Le Signal at the top of the Le Fornet cable car has a sun terrace, a log fire and a yurt for cold days. La Peau de Vache, halfway down La Face, is known for burgers big enough for two, and Le Refuge de Solaise serves gourmet food in a glass conservatory below the top of the Solaise gondola. Down in the village, La Baraque on the main street has live folk music and a following among locals.
